THIS CRIMINAL PETITION IS FILED UNDER SECTION 438 (FILED U/S.482 BNNS) CR.P.C PRAYING TO PASS AN ORDER GRANTING ANTICIPATORY BAIL THEREBY DIRECTING THE RESPONDENT MALLESWARAM POLICE TO RELEASE THE PETITIONER/ACCUSED NO.1 IN CR.NO.139/2024, FOR THE OFFENCE P/U/S 406, 420, 120(B), 504, 506 AND 34 OF IPC,
PENDING BEFORE THE COURT OF 3rd ACMM, BENGALURU IN THE EVENT OF PETITIONER BEING ARRESTED.
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE S VISHWAJITH SHETTY  ORAL ORDER Accused No.1 in Crime No.139/2024 registered by Malleshwaram Police Station, Bengaluru, for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 120-B, 504, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC, is before this Court under Section 438 of Cr.P.C, seeking anticipatory bail.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
3. FIR in Crime No.139/2024 was registered by Malleshwaram Police Station, Bengaluru, against the petitioner and 4 others for the aforesaid offences on the basis of the first information dated 11.09.2024 received NC: 2024:KHC:51205 from Smt.Shabhistan Gafur W/o. Abdul Gafur.
Apprehending arrest in the said case, the petitioner had filed Crl.Misc.No.9468/2024 before the Jurisdictional Sessions Court and the same was rejected on 04.11.2024.
Therefore, he is before this Court 4.
Sri V. Lakshminarayana, learned Senior counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that dispute between the parties appears to be is purely civil in nature.

Prior to the first informant approaching the Police, a notice dated 24.05.2024 was issued by her to the petitioner and reading of the said notice makes it very apparent that dispute between the parties is civil in nature.
By giving a criminal texture to the civil dispute, efforts are being made for recovery of the alleged dues.
He submits that the petitioner has not received any amount from the first informant.

He is ready and willing to Dr Bennet Abraham vs State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109302569/
2 co-operate with the Police for the purpose of investigation.

sentences.text: Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
Per contra, learned HCGP for respondent No.1 and learned counsel for respondent No.2-de-facto complainant have opposed the bail application by filing statement of objections.
They submit that the petitioner is a person having criminal antecedents and similar other criminal cases are pending against the petitioner.
In the present case, the first informant has paid more than Rs.7.00 Crores of money for purchase of land for the purpose of establishing a medical college.
However, no land has been purchased by the accused persons and they have cheated the first informant.
Accordingly, they pray to dismiss the petition.

6. Perusal of the first information dated 11.09.2024 submitted by the de-facto complainant, which has resulted in registering FIR in crime No.139/2024 against the petitioner and other accused persons would go to show that the dispute between the parties is prima facie civil in nature.

In the first information itself, a mention is made about a notice issued by the first informant to the NC:
2024:KHC:51205 petitioner.

Copy of said notice dated 24.05.2024 addressed to the petitioner sent by first informant is made available to the Court along with a memo dated 28.11.2024.
7.

Perusal of the said notice would go to show that the parties have entered into certain agreement and in the notice it is alleged that there is a breach of contract and a claim is made for the payment of the outstanding dues.
A request is made in the said notice to settle the unpaid dues.

After issuing the aforesaid legal notice contemplating legal action against the petitioner in the event he fails to pay the dues as claimed in the notice dated 24.05.2024, the present criminal case has been registered against the petitioner and others on the basis of first information received from the first informant.
The alleged offences are triable by the Court of Magistrate.
The maximum punishment for the alleged offences is imprisonment for a period of seven years.

Merely for the reason that there are other criminal cases pending against the petitioner, same cannot be a ground to refuse the bail NC: 2024:KHC:51205 as sought for in the petition if the petitioner is otherwise otherwise found entitled for the said relief under the circumstances, I am of the opinion that the prayer made by the petitioner for grant of anticipatory bail is required to be answered affirmatively.

8. Accordingly, the following:
ORDER
The Criminal Petition is allowed.

The Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer between 10.00 a.m.
and 11.30 a.m. on 16.12.2024 and on the said date, if necessary the Investigating Officer is at liberty to take the petitioner to custody for the NC: 2024:KHC:51205 Dr Bennet Abraham vs State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109302569/
3 purpose of interrogation.
